paragraphs.source_en: Early the next morning, Naruse Masanari quietly boarded a large thirty-koku boat. Boats belonging to the Chaya and Suminokura houses were also due to sail, but he had deliberately chosen this one because no one aboard knew him. He had only one young attendant with him, while most of the passengers were merchants. Before the boat departed, the passengers merely exchanged common street gossip. Masanari hoped to seize the opportunity to learn what ordinary people thought of the shogunate.
